newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares firm ahead of censure motion vote.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares firm ahead of censure motion vote.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted gains in weak volume on Tuesday ahead of a preliminary vote in parliament on a censure motion against the Islamist-led coaliton government, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,510, up 18 points, or 1.21 percent from Friday. The market was closed on Monday.
Trade volume fell sharply to 12.79 trillion lira ($92.5 million) from Friday's 17.67 trillion ($128.4 million).

"If it is accepted in today's preliminary vote that the censure motion will go ahead, the market will open higher on Wednesday. But it will still await the final vote for the government to fall," said Taner Mirza from Es securities.

A simple majority of those in parliament are needed for the motion to go forward to a full debate on Thursday and a further no-confidence vote on Saturday. But Turkish political tradition dicates a government resign if it loses the first round.
"Liquidity inflow to the market has weakened when compared to last week. Activity is still speculative and the market can easily react to negative news," said Mirza.

Brokers said news that the small far-right Islamist party BBP pledged support for the government in today's preliminary vote prompted sales in early afternoon trade, causing the index to drop from a high of 1,518.

The decision of the BBP which has seven deputies could swing the tight vote in favour of the Islamist-led alliance which has 280 deputies in the 550-seat parliament. The opposition has said they had some support from the coalition's conservative wing.
The government has been losing blood heavily since the secularist military began pushing it in February to stamp out rising Islamist activism.
